.github/workflows/ci.yml: # Continuous integration with an SSDLC gate at every stage. See SSDLC.md.
# Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs; the workflow token is read-only.
# One run per change (PRO-202): a push to a branch with an open pull request used to start a push run and a
# pull_request run on the same commit (different refs, so different concurrency groups). Branches now run on
# their pull request; main on push; a branch without a pull request by workflow_dispatch on its ref.
# labeled/unlabeled: the go-api job reads the `api-break` label from the event, and a re-run keeps the
# labels of its original event, so a label change starts a run of its own
- cron: "17 3 * * 1"   # weekly re-run catches toolchain drift and new advisories on an unchanged tree
# A pull request or dispatched run cancels its superseded run on the same ref. A push to main gets a group of its
# own commit, so no main run is ever cancelled or dropped while queued: every main commit keeps its own gate
# result, which the release checks read for a tagged commit.
group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.ref }}
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Build the Go binary the launcher tests run (make go-build, offline and vendored; nothing to build without the target)
- name: Compile every module (syntax gate, no runtime dependencies allowed)
grep -q '^dependencies = \[\]' pyproject.toml || (echo "runtime dependencies are not allowed" && exit 1)
- name: Repository tooling and launcher tests (the Python reference engine is removed, PRO-403)
python -B -m unittest discover -q 2> test-output.txt || (cat test-output.txt && exit 1)
- name: Documentation numbers must match the tree (families, applications, tests, version)
- name: Product integrity (build manifest, key logs, content lock)
- name: Presentation suite (Node and browser tests are required in presentation-ui)
# `unittest` passes a skipped test, so the strict runner fails on any skip but the two UI tests named
# here, which the presentation-ui job runs with Node and Playwright and allows no skip at all.
- name: Offline replay of synthetic captures through the launcher and the Go binary
# The presentation suite with every prerequisite installed explicitly: Node and the lock-pinned
# Playwright with its Chromium. No test may skip, so a missing prerequisite fails the job instead of
# reading as a pass. PRO-403: the page is served by the Go binary; there is no wheel to install.
name: presentation with Node and a real browser (no test may skip)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Build the Go binary the launcher tests run (make go-build, offline and vendored; nothing to build without the target)
- name: Install Playwright with Chromium from the lock
- name: Presentation suite from the checkout, every test required (store unit tests in Node, the dashboard in Chromium)
bandit -c bandit.yaml -r protodetect.py main.py -f txt | tee bandit.txt
- name: Set up Go for the pinned scanner builds
- name: Secret scan (gitleaks 8.30.1, full history, inline allows ignored)
# tools/scanners/go.mod and go.sum pin gitleaks and every dependency (checked against the Go
# checksum database; rule 16 locks go.mod). Only those two files are copied to RUNNER_TEMP and
# built there, read-only. --ignore-gitleaks-allow makes gitleaks itself ignore inline allow
# comments in every commit it scans (item 21); .gitleaks.toml (rule 16) is the only allowlist.
- name: The gitleaks allowlists stay narrow (tools/check_gitleaks_allowlist.py, the pinned gitleaks)
# After the scan, so no repository code runs before the scanner (rule 15). A CNAME chain is allowed only in
# research/live-results-*.tsv, and keys, tokens and the same chain elsewhere must still be reported.
- name: Every action must be pinned to a commit SHA
- name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM for the package (zero runtime dependencies expected)
echo "pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency (checked by tools/sbom_summary.py)."
fetch-depth: 0   # rule 16 searches every commit gitleaks scans, back to its baseline
- name: Fetch actionlint 1.7.7 and verify its published checksum
- name: Lint every workflow (syntax, expressions, shellcheck-style script checks)
echo "actionlint: $(find .github/workflows -name '*.yml' | wc -l) workflow files clean" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
- name: Audit every workflow for security weaknesses (zizmor, pedantic persona, offline audits)
# Template injection, credential persistence, cache poisoning, excessive or undocumented
# permissions, unpinned or superfluous actions, missing concurrency limits. Any finding fails.
# It runs before any repository code in this job (tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 15),
# so no repository script can shadow it through the runner's per-step path file.
- name: Workflow policy (gate covers every ci job, drift gate triggers on every workflow, releases serialize, tags must be on main)
- name: Cross-check the workflow policy parser against PyYAML (any disagreement is a policy blind spot)
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 11 pins this step (it installs its own hash-pinned toolchain).
name: known vulnerabilities in the dev toolchain (pip-audit, govulncheck)
- name: Install the hash-pinned toolchain (pip-audit included)
- name: Audit every pinned development dependency against the advisory databases
run: pip-audit -r requirements-dev.txt --require-hashes --strict --progress-spinner off --desc on | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
- name: Set up Go for the pinned scanner builds
- name: Audit the Go-built scanners against the Go vulnerability database (govulncheck)
# The same pinned build as the secret scan (tools/scanners), checked symbol by symbol: any known
# vulnerability reachable in gitleaks or govulncheck, in a dependency or the Go standard library
# it was built with, fails the job (item 22).
- name: Audit the Go engine module against the Go vulnerability database (govulncheck, vendored source)
# Ported from the engine lane's 34ea6b0 (claude/go-migration), so ci.yml keeps one writer. Source mode
# follows the call graph of every package in go/, on exactly the committed vendor tree
# (GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor; with no dependency, as on main today, the module alone): a known
# vulnerability reachable in a dependency or in the pinned standard library fails the job. Modules
# are never fetched (GOPROXY=off); govulncheck reads only its vulnerability database (vuln.go.dev).
# Known vulnerabilities in every committed lockfile (Python requirements, npm, the engine's go.mod and every CI
# tool module) from the OSV database: osv-scanner 2.7.1, built from tools/golint/osv-scanner/go.mod and go.sum
# (every module hash checked against the Go checksum database) in a copy outside the checkout before any
# repository code runs. A finding fails unless tools/osv_ignore.json accepts it for that lockfile and package,
# with a reason and an expiry; an expired or stale entry fails too (tools/osv_scan.py, item 41). govulncheck
# (toolchain-audit) stays the reachability check for Go.
name: Known vulnerabilities in every lockfile (osv-scanner; accepted only with a reason and an expiry)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Scan every lockfile against the OSV database (tools/osv_scan.py)
# Migration M10: the Go engine's own gate on GitHub's runners, on the one Go toolchain the scanner
# builds use (tools/check_go_drift.py keeps it the newest patch of a supported line; tools/go_ci.py
# refuses a go/go.mod that builds with another: its `toolchain` line, else its `go` line). `make
# go-check` runs in three jobs (PRO-202): this one (`make go-check-static`: gofmt, go vet, the mutation
# boundary checks; then `make go-check-race`: go test -race; then `make go-check-386`: the protocol
# parsers' tests on GOARCH=386, where 32-bit int wraps such as SEC-X509-1 show; PRO-262), go-fuzz-smoke (`make go-check-fuzz`, one
# shard per matrix job) and go-parity (`make go-check-parity`). Each part is the same Makefile target
# `make go-check` runs locally, so the three jobs check exactly what one did. A commit without the
# migration tree has nothing to check and says so in the summary; one with part of it fails.
# Docs-only fast path (PRO-202 step 3): this job, go-fuzz-smoke, go-parity, go-minimum and go-determinism
# pass --docs-only-fast-path and check out both parents of the merge commit; on a pull request whose every
# changed path is Markdown or research data (tools/ci_scope.py) they check the tree and toolchain, skip
# the make target and list the paths, so the job and the gate still report success. A push to main,
# the schedule, a dispatch or any doubt runs everything. No job-level `if:` (rule 13).
# GOPROXY=off: the engine's dependency is vendored, so a target asking for any other Go or module
# fails instead of downloading it mid-job.
name: Go engine (gofmt, vet, race tests)
fetch-depth: 2   # both parents of the pull request merge commit (tools/ci_scope.py)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: gofmt, go vet and the mutation boundary checks (make go-check-static)
# The fuzz smoke of `make go-check`: every GO_FUZZ_SMOKE target in the Makefile for its seconds, split
# into shards by tools/go_fuzz_smoke.py (longest first to the least-loaded shard, fixed, so the shards
# are disjoint and together run every target). The matrix must list every shard "1/N" .. "N/N":
# The shard reaches the tool through the environment, never expanded into the script.
fetch-depth: 2   # both parents of the pull request merge commit (tools/ci_scope.py)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Fuzz smoke, one shard (make go-check-fuzz GO_FUZZ_SHARD)

name: Go parity with the Python reference (replay, analyze, decrypt, live, schema, random, bench)
fetch-depth: 2   # both parents of the pull request merge commit (tools/ci_scope.py)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Parity gates (make go-check-parity) and parity report floor

name: Go engine on its declared minimum Go (vet, race tests)

- name: Read the declared minimum Go
- name: Set up the declared minimum Go
- name: Go engine on its minimum (make go-check-minimum)

- name: Set up the pinned Go

- name: Set up the pinned Go

- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Check the engine's dependency licences (tools/go_deep.py)

- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Measure coverage and hold the floors (tools/go_cover.py)

name: Go API compatibility (apidiff; public breaks need the api-break label)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Compare the module API with the base (tools/go_api.py)

name: External contract compatibility (JSON schemas, protodetect CLI; breaks need the api-break label)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Compare the schemas and the CLI with the base (tools/contract_check.py)

name: content pack (lock, release history, ids, Python/Go parity)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Build the Go binary the referenced Python tests run (offline and vendored)

- name: Every security requirement names tests that exist and pass when run (none skipped)

name: ledgers (generated sections not hand-edited, notes well-formed)

.github/workflows/ledgers.yml: # Nightly ledger check (PRO-347, SSDLC item 43): the shared ledger sections are generated from
# migration/notes/PRO-<n>.md by tools/build_ledgers.py. Pull requests never regenerate them (that is what made
# them conflict), so main lags after each merge. This job runs the strict check on a full clone of main, fails
# when it is behind with the command to run, and uploads the exact refresh patch and the rebuilt files.
# Read-only: the token is `contents: read`, checkout keeps no credential, and nothing is pushed or opened.
# Opening the docs-only refresh pull request from here is Lee's decision on a policy exception (SSDLC item 43).
# GitHub runs `schedule` from the default branch's copy of this file; on a branch, use workflow_dispatch.
name: generated ledger sections are current (strict; refresh patch as an artifact)
fetch-depth: 0   # the pull request that merged each note comes from the merge history
- name: Rebuild the generated sections and keep the patch
- name: Upload the refresh patch and the rebuilt files
- name: Strict check (fails while main is behind; apply the patch above as a docs-only pull request)
.github/workflows/merge-readiness.yml: # Daily merge-readiness report: a trial merge of claude/go-migration into main inside the
# runner (tools/merge_readiness.py, `git merge-tree --write-tree`), reported in the job summary
# as clean or conflicting with every conflicting file. Report only: the job never pushes,
# comments or opens anything, the token is `contents: read` and checkout keeps no credential.
# GitHub runs `schedule` from the default branch's copy of this file; a change on a branch is
# proven with `workflow_dispatch` on that branch (the workflow is registered, so dispatch works).
name: trial merge of claude/go-migration into main (report only)
.github/workflows/nightly-fuzz.yml: # Extended seeded fuzzing beyond the unit-test budget. Findings are regressions in
# bounded parsing (crash, unbounded work, status outside the documented set).
# Three jobs (PRO-403: the Python mutation fuzz went with the Python reference engine): every Go fuzz
# target for minutes instead of the per-push gate's seconds (tools/go_fuzz_long.py; failing inputs are uploaded);
# the randomized opening properties, Go only (make property-long, PRO-401: it replaced the
# randomized Python-vs-Go parity run when the Python reference was removed; the rapid failfiles of a
# failing run, which reproduce it, are uploaded); and mutation testing of the Go parser packages
# with gremlins against migration/mutation/baseline.json (make mutation, PRO-176; its results are
# uploaded on every run as trend data).
# None of them is a required check, so a nightly failure never blocks a pull request.
# GitHub runs `schedule` only from the default branch's copy of this file, so a change here
# takes effect nightly once it is on main; before that, run it with workflow_dispatch on
# the branch (the file already exists on main, so dispatch can target any ref).
description: minutes of Go fuzzing, split across every fuzz target (1-100)
description: seed of the randomized opening properties (digits; empty means this run's id)
cancel-in-progress: false   # a manual run never cancels the scheduled one; they queue
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
name: extended Go fuzz (every fuzz target)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Fuzz every Go fuzz target
# The ci Go jobs' environment: no download of any module or toolchain (dependencies are
# vendored, go_ci.go_env sets -mod=vendor then), on exactly the pinned compiler.
# make property-long (go/internal/engine/openings_property_test.go, PRO-401): generated TLS ClientHellos,
# HTTP/1 request heads, SSH identification lines and protected QUIC v1/v2 client Initials whose identity is
# known by construction, checked without an oracle: identified as built, split invariant and deterministic,
# never another identity when truncated, under a wrong hint or under a tight budget. The seed is this run's
# id (or the dispatch input) and is written to the summary: the same seed and count reproduce the run exactly
# (make property-long PROPERTY_SEED=<seed> CHECKS=<count>), and a failure's rapid failfile is uploaded.
name: randomized opening properties, Go only (long)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
# The ci Go jobs' environment: no module or toolchain download (vendored tree, pinned compiler).
# The dispatch inputs reach make only after they are checked to be plain decimal numbers.
[[ "$SEED" =~ ^[0-9]{1,18}$ ]] || { echo "seed must be digits, got: $SEED"; exit 2; }
echo "### Randomized opening properties ($CHECKS draws each, seed $SEED)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
make property-long PROPERTY_SEED="$SEED" CHECKS="$CHECKS" 2>&1 | tee property-long.txt || status=1
- name: Upload the failing draws (rapid failfiles and the log)
# make mutation (migration/mutation/mutation.py, PRO-126/PRO-176): gremlins mutates each Go parser package
# (arithmetic, comparison boundaries, negated conditions) and runs that package's tests against every covered
# mutant. The job fails only when a package's efficacy (killed / (killed + lived)) falls more than 5 points
# below migration/mutation/baseline.json, or a baseline package has no result. The 5 points are
# mutation.py's TOLERANCE, a placeholder until Research Lab's stability check (PRO-173) recommends a value.
# The one step with module-proxy access builds gremlins v0.6.0 (Apache-2.0; its dependencies are MIT,
# BSD-3-Clause or Apache-2.0) from a RUNNER_TEMP copy of its pin module, and fills the module cache from a
# copy of go/go.mod and go/go.sum (gremlins runs `go mod download` before it measures coverage), every hash
# checked against go.sum and the checksum database, before any repository code runs. Everything after it is
# offline: GOPROXY=off, the pinned compiler, and the engine built from go/vendor (mutation.py sets -mod=vendor).
name: Go mutation testing (gremlins, against the baseline)
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Build gremlins v0.6.0 from its pin module and fill the module cache (the only networked step)
- name: Mutation testing of the Go parsers against the baseline (make mutation)
# The ci Go jobs' environment: no module or toolchain download (the cache filled above, the vendored
# tree, the pinned compiler). MUTATION_BIN makes make run the binary built above instead of installing one.
run: make mutation PYTHON=python MUTATION_BIN="$MUTATION_BIN" MUTATION_ARGS="--summary $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
- name: Upload the mutation results (every run, for the efficacy trend)
.github/workflows/perf-history.yml: # Performance history: each main run records the existing measurements (tools/perf_profile.py's CPU,
# memory and bytes-to-identification sections, and any Go benchmark) and compares them with the median
# of the previous comparable runs (tools/perf_history.py documents the thresholds: bytes and counts fail
# above +10 %, timings warn above +30 % and fail above +100 %). The store is this workflow's artifacts:
# the history of the newest successful run on the same branch is downloaded, extended and uploaded
# again (90 days). A failing run uploads nothing, so a regression never becomes the baseline; dispatch
# with accept_regression=true to record an intended change. Read-only token; nothing is pushed.
# The push trigger on main is the activation; a change on a branch is proven with workflow_dispatch
# on that branch (the workflow is registered, so dispatch works).
description: record this run's numbers as the baseline even if they regress (true or false)
actions: read   # list this workflow's earlier runs and download their history artifact
# One run per branch at a time, never cancelled, so the history is a single chain.
name: record and compare the performance measurements
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Measure (perf_profile cpu, bytes, memory; Go benchmarks when there are any)
- name: Fetch the history of the newest successful run on this branch
RUN=$(gh run list --repo "$GH_REPO" --workflow perf-history.yml --branch "$BRANCH" --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId // empty')
echo "no earlier successful run on $BRANCH: this run starts the history" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
- name: Compare with the baseline (fails on a regression beyond the thresholds)
- name: Upload the history for the next run
.github/workflows/publish-release.yml: # Guarded release controller. A `v*` tag builds the reproducible Go
# binaries with their SBOM in a read-only job, then a separate job holding the write scopes
# attests (Sigstore-signed provenance) and publishes exactly the files the build job produced. workflow_dispatch and changes to this file or its helper run the build job
# alone (a dry run that never publishes), so the release path is exercised before the
# first real tag; a dry run also signs its provenance with an ephemeral key into a separate,
# never-published artifact. See docs/RELEASING.md and SSDLC.md.
# This file replaces .github/workflows/release.yml. A tag push runs the workflow file found
# at the tagged commit, so every older commit's release.yml still publishes a matching tag
# without the provenance check; that legacy path must be disabled in the repository's
# Actions settings (SSDLC.md, "Enforced controls"), and tools/check_workflow_policy.py keeps
# the path from coming back so disabling it never disables this controller.
# Per ref: a dry run or a re-run of one tag never cancels that ref's run in flight. Different
# tags get different groups here, so the publish job carries its own constant group below.
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
# The provenance and release checks run in a fresh job of pinned actions and these two
# steps only, so no earlier step and no repository test can change the PATH or the
# environment their `gh` and `python` run under (the runner's file commands carry such
# changes to later steps of the same job). tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 4 pins
# this whole job: keys, permissions, runner and every step, in order.
contents: read   # checkout and the compare API for the provenance check
actions: read    # the tagged commit's workflow runs for the release checks gate
- name: Check out the commit being released
- name: A release tag must point at a commit already on main
# Tag protection is not enforceable on this plan (SSDLC.md), so the workflow checks it:
# compare/${SHA}...${MAIN} is "identical" or "ahead" only when main contains the commit. MAIN is the SHA of
# refs/heads/main (git/ref is an exact match), never the bare name, which a tag named main would shadow
# (SEC-CI-1); a failed lookup leaves an all-zero SHA, which the compare rejects, so a tag fails closed.
# A tag fails closed on any other answer; dry runs report only. The pull-request head,
# not GitHub's synthetic merge commit, is what a dry run compares.
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 4 pins this step's env and run lines exactly.
- name: The tagged commit's ci and CodeQL workflows must have passed
# Required checks are not enforceable on this plan (SSDLC.md), and the build job re-runs
# the test gate but not CodeQL. Only push runs of ci.yml and codeql.yml (by workflow path)
# for this exact commit count, never a job name another workflow could reuse; a tag
# fails closed on a missing, pending or failed run; dry runs report only.
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 4 pins this step's env and run lines exactly.

gh api --paginate "repos/${GH_REPO}/actions/runs?head_sha=${SHA}&per_page=100" --jq '.workflow_runs[] | {path, name, event, status, conclusion, head_sha, updated_at}' > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/workflow-runs.jsonl" || echo "api-error" > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/workflow-runs.jsonl"
# Read-only: the gate, the version check, the Go binaries, the SBOMs
# and the checksums. Nothing in this job can write to the repository.
name: release build (gate, version check, distributions, SBOM, checksums)
fetch-depth: 0   # build_ledgers.py reads the pull request that merged each note from the merge history
- name: Set up the pinned Go
- name: Build the Go binary the launcher tests run (make go-build, offline and vendored; nothing to build without the target)
# PRO-402: `protodetect analyze`, `live` and `serve` run only the Go binary, so the unit tests below need it
# (as in ci.yml); without it test_policy and test_schema exit 2 (PRO-480). go/bin/ is ignored by git and is
# not a release file; the release binaries come from tools/build_go_release.py below.
- name: The full gate must pass on the commit being released
# tools/check_docs_counts.py: a tag fails on a documented test count that lags the tree (--strict), so a
# release never ships a stale count. A dry run (a pull request or a branch push) runs it without --strict,
# because main's generated counts lag by design after each merge (PRO-347) and a pull request does not
# regenerate them; it still fails on family, application and version drift (PRO-480).
- name: The generated ledgers must be current for a tag release
# tools/build_ledgers.py: a release must not ship stale "Recent work" sections or test counts, so a tag
# runs --check --strict (it needs the full history checked out above). A dry run (a pull request or a branch
# push) runs the lag-tolerant --check, because a pull request's own note only reaches the generated sections
# in the refresh after it merges; it still fails on a hand edit, a malformed note or a broken marker.
- name: The reported version must equal pyproject.toml, and the tag when there is one
DECLARED=$(python -c 'import re; print(re.search(r"^version = \"([^\"]+)\"", open("pyproject.toml", encoding="utf-8").read(), re.M).group(1))')
test "${VERSION}" = "${DECLARED}" || (echo "protodetect reports ${VERSION} but pyproject.toml declares ${DECLARED}" && exit 1)
test "v${VERSION}" = "${TAG}" || (echo "tag ${TAG} does not match version ${VERSION}" && exit 1)
- name: The runner's gh supports every attestation flag the publish job verifies with
# The publish job only runs for a real tag; this dry-runnable check keeps an image change
# from first surfacing as a failed release.
grep -q -- "$flag" <<<"$HELP" || { echo "$(gh --version) lacks gh attestation verify $flag"; exit 1; }
echo "gh attestation verify flags present" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
- name: Reproducible Go binaries (five targets, each built twice and compared) and their SBOM
# tools/build_go_release.py: CGO off, -trimpath, no VCS stamp, no build id, on the pinned Go with
# GOPROXY=off and the vendor tree; the SBOM comes from the binaries' own build information.
# PRO-403: the product is the Go binaries above (their SBOM comes from their build information); the Python
# wheel, its decryption extra and the product SBOM of that wheel went with the Python reference engine.
- name: Dry-run provenance, signed with a key generated for this run (a separate artifact, never published)
# The real signature is the publish job's Sigstore attestation, which a dry run must not create
# (it writes to the public transparency log); this proves the statement, signing and verification.
- name: Keep the dry-run provenance and signature for review
- name: Hand the exact files to the publish job
# Only a pushed `v*` tag reaches this job; dry runs stop after the build. It checks out
# nothing: it attests and publishes the build job's files after re-verifying their checksums.
# One constant group for every tag: publishes of different tags never overlap, and one in
# flight is never cancelled. GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so a third tag pushed
# while one publishes and another waits replaces the waiting one, which ends cancelled
# (nothing published) and is re-run by hand. tools/check_workflow_policy.py enforces this.
contents: write       # gh release create uploads the distributions to the release
id-token: write       # OIDC token for the Sigstore signing of the provenance attestation
attestations: write   # attest-build-provenance stores the attestation on the repository
- name: Fetch the build job's files
- name: The files must still match the checksums the build job recorded
- name: Every file's attestation must verify before anything is published
# Binds each file to this controller workflow, this tag and commit, and a GitHub-hosted
# runner; a missing or partial attestation fails the release before gh release create.
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 8 pins every step of this job, in order (an allowlist).
- name: Publish the release with the runner's gh CLI (no third-party action)
.github/workflows/release-audit.yml: # Scheduled release audit: a detective control no tag can bypass. A tag push runs the workflow
# file at the tagged commit, so an older commit's unguarded release.yml (or a workflow edited on
# a branch) can still publish; a scheduled run always uses the default branch's copy of this
# file. It fails, and GitHub notifies the owner, when a v* tag points off main or a published
# release is not bound to a current, on-main v* tag and its commit, or has an asset (hidden files
# included) without an attestation from publish-release.yml for that tag and commit. Read-only.
# Schedules only run from the default branch, so this takes effect once merged to main; pushes
# that change it run it as a dry run against the real releases. See SSDLC.md.
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
name: release audit (v* tags on main, every asset attested by the controller)
contents: read       # list tags and releases, compare refs, download release assets
attestations: read   # gh attestation verify reads the repository's attestations
- name: Gather facts about every v* tag and published release, then decide
jq -nc --arg main "$main" --rawfile others "$RUNNER_TEMP/main-refs.txt" '{kind: "main", tag: "main", main: $main, others: $others}' >> "$facts"
jq -nc --arg tag "$tag" --arg compare "$status" --arg commit "$commit" '{kind: "tag", tag: $tag, compare: $compare, commit: $commit}' >> "$facts"
if gh release download "$tag" --dir "$dir"; then download=ok; else download=error; fi
jq -nc --arg tag "$tag" --arg commit "$commit" --arg download "$download" --argjson assets "$count" '{kind: "release", tag: $tag, commit: $commit, assets: $assets, download: $download}' >> "$facts"

if gh attestation verify "$file" --repo "$GH_REPO" --signer-workflow "$GH_REPO/.github/workflows/publish-release.yml" --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" --source-digest "$commit" --deny-self-hosted-runners > /dev/null; then verified=true; else verified=false; fi
jq -nc --arg tag "$tag" --arg asset "$(basename "$file")" --argjson verified "$verified" '{kind: "asset", tag: $tag, asset: $asset, verified: $verified}' >> "$facts"
.github/workflows/scorecard.yml: # Weekly OpenSSF Scorecard: the repository's supply-chain posture (pinned dependencies, token
# permissions, dangerous workflow patterns, branch protection, code review, SAST, fuzzing, and
# more), uploaded as SARIF to code scanning and kept as an artifact. publish_results stays false:
# publishing to the public Scorecard API needs `id-token: write` and a workflow with no top-level
# `defaults:`, which the workflow policy (rules 5 and 6) forbids outside the release controller.
name: OpenSSF Scorecard (weekly, SARIF to code scanning)
security-events: write   # upload-sarif writes the results to code scanning (no-op until enabled)
actions: read            # Scorecard reads workflow runs for the CI-Tests and Dangerous-Workflow checks
- name: Run Scorecard (results stay private to this repository)
- name: Upload to code scanning (requires the feature to be enabled)
.github/workflows/supply-chain-drift.yml: # Weekly supply-chain drift gate: the pinned action SHAs must still be the commits their
# tag comments name, the checksum-verified tool downloads must still resolve, and every
# hash in requirements-dev.txt must still match what the index serves, and the Go that builds
# the pinned scanners must be a supported line on its newest patch. A failure here
# means a tag moved, a release disappeared or an index artifact changed: a review item,
# never something to fix by re-pinning blindly. See SSDLC.md.
- ".github/workflows/**"   # every workflow holds pinned actions; tools/check_workflow_policy.py enforces this
- "tools/go_ci.py"          # check_go_drift.py reads both go.mod files through it
- ".github/workflows/**"   # every workflow holds pinned actions; tools/check_workflow_policy.py enforces this
- "tools/go_ci.py"          # check_go_drift.py reads both go.mod files through it
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
name: pinned action SHAs still match their tags
- name: Every action must be pinned to a commit SHA (same gate as ci)
- name: Resolve every tag comment against its repository and compare with the pinned SHA
name: tool downloads and dev-dependency hashes still resolve
- name: The actionlint release ci.yml names must still match the SHA-256 ci.yml verifies
# The version and checksum are read from ci.yml itself, so this job always checks the
# values the workflow-lint job will use rather than a second copy of them.
- name: Every hash-pinned development dependency must still download and match its hash
python -m pip download --require-hashes --no-deps -r requirements-dev.txt -d downloads > download.log
echo "downloaded and hash-verified ${COUNT} distributions from requirements-dev.txt"
echo "${COUNT} distributions downloaded with \`--require-hashes\`; every hash matched."
- name: The pinned pip-audit still installs and runs from the verified downloads alone
name: the Go that builds the pinned scanners is supported and on its newest patch
- name: The setup-go version is one Go release, a supported line, on its newest patch
# Read from the Go module proxy's toolchain list; govulncheck in ci covers known
# vulnerabilities, this covers a release line or patch level that has fallen behind.
